The Flutter docs draw the line.
, also called UI state or local state, "is the state you can neatly contain in a single widget": the current page of a

, the progress of an animation, the selected tab. Other parts of the tree seldom need it, you don't serialize it, and it doesn't change in complex ways, so "there is no need to use state management techniques" on it. "All you need is a StatefulWidget."
is the rest: state you share across many parts of the app and keep between sessions, such as login info, user preferences, notifications or a shopping cart. That's where a library earns its place.
The docs are honest that the line moves. You can even manage all of an app's state with
, they note, as the starter app from

does. The selected tab can become app state if other code must change it or it must survive a restart, and state that started ephemeral may need to move as the app grows. They quote Redux's author, Dan Abramov, for the rule of thumb: "Do whatever is less awkward."
